intro: Choose the observable that can answer the question, then open the existing task that produces or tests it. All target calculations assume a trustworthy model, method, numerical baseline, and reference state.
boundary: These routes are independent starting points, not a new taxonomy or a required sequence. A result may send the study back to the model, method, reference state, or target calculation.

questions.question: Have the declared geometry-optimization conditions been satisfied?
questions.required_observable: Accepted coordinates, every relevant force component, stress for relaxed cell degrees of freedom, and evidence that the electronic state remained the intended one.
questions.prerequisites: Declare the computational model, active degrees of freedom, constraints, electronic state, and numerical baseline before optimization.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This guide defines the active coordinates and constraints before a run; it does not prove that a minimum has been found.

questions.validation_requirement: Inspect every free force component rather than only an aggregate force, the relevant stress components, the final geometry, electronic convergence, and state identity. Audit the accepted structure again in the fixed-geometry reference calculation.
questions.claim_limitation: A local optimization does not establish the global minimum, dynamical stability, thermodynamic stability, or an experimental structure.
questions.common_human_route: Open the structure in a viewer, inspect the cell and constraints, then prepare, monitor, and re-open the optimization in the selected code.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect geometry before and after, force/stress history, every free force component, warnings, step behavior, and physical plausibility.

questions.question: What is the formation or reaction energy?
questions.required_observable: A normalized energy or free-energy difference for an explicitly balanced reaction and declared reference states.
questions.prerequisites: Use compatible composition accounting, evaluator, charge and spin treatment, numerical settings, state identities, and thermodynamic convention for every term.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This is a synthetic A2B3 ledger fixture. It demonstrates the comparability gate but does not provide a real material formation-energy result or validate the underlying energies and reference states.

questions.validation_requirement: Check reaction balance, normalization, reference-state identity, numerical convergence of every term, and sensitivity to defensible reference choices.
questions.claim_limitation: A negative formation energy does not establish convex-hull stability, synthesis, kinetic accessibility, or experimental formation.
questions.common_human_route: Find reference phases in literature or databases, calculate comparable states, then assemble and plot the energy ledger in a spreadsheet, notebook, or transparent script.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect reference identities, stoichiometry, units, magnetic and structural states, numerical sensitivity, and energy-difference outliers.

questions.question: Is this composition stable against decomposition?
questions.required_observable: Energy above a lower convex envelope constructed from a sufficiently complete competing-phase set at common thermodynamic conditions.

related_topics.context: For same-composition phases as a function of pressure, use this route instead of a composition hull.

questions.prerequisites: Prepare comparable formation energies, consistent composition normalization, a declared chemical system and thermodynamic convention, and an inspectable candidate phase set.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This is a derived-public-data Li-P worked example, not a guide for importing and validating a new project's complete phase set.

questions.validation_requirement: Challenge candidate-set completeness, phase-set sensitivity, energy normalization, numerical convergence, and reasonable method choices.
questions.claim_limitation: Hull membership is conditional on the declared phase set, thermodynamic conditions, and energy model. It does not establish kinetic stability, synthesis, finite-temperature stability, or dynamical stability.
questions.common_human_route: Build the competing-phase set from databases and literature, inspect every identity, then construct the hull with a phase-diagram tool, notebook, or reviewed script.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect the lower envelope, tie lines, omitted or duplicate phases, reference consistency, near-degenerate competitors, and phase-set sensitivity.

questions.question: Is the reference state metallic?
questions.required_observable: Converged full-zone electronic sampling around the Fermi level, supported by a converged density of states referenced to the same Fermi level.

related_topics.context: Use a converged density of states near the same Fermi level as supporting evidence.

questions.prerequisites: Use a qualified reference state, adequate band coverage, uniform full-zone sampling, declared occupations or smearing, and one consistent Fermi-energy convention.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This bounded real Aluminium comparison does not claim that its stored full-zone sample is converged.

questions.validation_requirement: Test k-point sampling, smearing, band coverage, full-zone extrema or crossings, density-of-states broadening, and energy-zero consistency.
questions.claim_limitation: A high-symmetry band path alone is not full-Brillouin-zone evidence of metallicity, and a broadened finite density of states on one mesh can be a numerical artifact.
questions.common_human_route: Establish the reference state, run dense full-zone sampling for DOS or Fermi-surface evidence, and use a band-path plot only as a complementary selected-dispersion view.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect states at the Fermi level, mesh and broadening sensitivity, occupations, full-zone crossings or surfaces, spin channels, and DOS/path disagreement.

questions.question: Is the structure dynamically stable in the harmonic approximation?
questions.required_observable: A qualified harmonic phonon spectrum over the q-space domain required by the claim, with apparent imaginary modes challenged against numerical and acoustic-consistency errors.
questions.prerequisites: Start from a suitable reference geometry and electronic state, force-accurate numerical settings, tight response convergence, and an appropriate q-mesh or supercell representation.

first_action.evidence_boundary: Start with the full q-grid or supercell route in Software Bridge and inspect its structure, parent calculation, complete q-point or displacement/force ledger, dispersion, and suspicious eigenvectors. The linked Silicon Gamma-point ledger is only an optional bounded replay after those objects exist; it is not evidence of full-zone dynamical stability.

questions.validation_requirement: Test electronic thresholds, cutoff and k-point sampling, q mesh or supercell size, interpolation, acoustic modes, mode eigenvectors, and non-analytic treatment where applicable.
questions.claim_limitation: A Gamma-point result does not establish full-Brillouin-zone dynamical stability. Harmonic stability does not establish thermodynamic, anharmonic, or finite-temperature stability.
questions.common_human_route: Open the relaxed structure, choose DFPT or finite displacement, retain every input plus stdout and stderr, calculate a complete q mesh or one-to-one supercell force set, build the force constants and dispersion, then select and animate each suspicious eigenvector in a compatible viewer.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect the reference output, q-point ledger or displacement/force mapping, q2r.x/matdyn.x products or force-constant files, acoustic behavior, q- or supercell convergence, imaginary-mode location and eigenvector, symmetry, and reproducibility of the distortion.

questions.question: Could conventional phonon-mediated superconductivity be supported?
questions.required_observable: Qualified phonons, electron-phonon matrix elements, an Eliashberg spectral function, coupling strength, logarithmic phonon frequency, and a declared transition-temperature model.

related_topics.context: A qualified phonon parent is required before electron-phonon coupling.
Interpret a transition-temperature model only after the coupling observables are converged.

questions.prerequisites: Establish a metallic full-zone reference state, dynamically qualified phonons, sufficiently dense k and q sampling, and a declared broadening or delta-function treatment.

first_action.statement: No reviewed hands-on practical guide is published for electron-phonon coupling or conventional superconductivity. Begin by creating inspectable parent runs for metallic SCF/NSCF states and a complete phonon q grid, then follow the official Wannier90 and EPW interface route while retaining every input, stdout, stderr, save directory, dynamical-matrix set, .win/.amn/.mmn/.eig/.wout lineage, and EPW output before interpreting coupling or Tc.

questions.validation_requirement: Converge the phonons, matrix elements, k mesh, q mesh, interpolation, broadening, spectral function, coupling strength, logarithmic frequency, transition-temperature result, and Coulomb-parameter sensitivity separately.
questions.claim_limitation: A computed coupling strength or model transition temperature does not establish experimental superconductivity. An unstable or insufficiently sampled phonon parent invalidates the downstream claim.
questions.common_human_route: Run and inspect the metallic SCF/NSCF parent, complete ph.x q-grid parent, Wannier90 preprocessing/localization/interface products, and epw.x interpolation in separate traceable stages; only then plot linewidths, alpha-squared-F, cumulative lambda, omega-log, and the declared Tc model.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect stdout and stderr at every stage, prefix/outdir and save-directory ancestry, direct versus interpolated bands and phonons, Wannier spreads and disentanglement, k/q meshes, broadenings, linewidths, alpha-squared-F, cumulative lambda, omega-log, Coulomb-parameter sensitivity, and derived-result stability.

questions.question: Which surface termination is energetically favored?
questions.required_observable: Comparable surface energies for explicitly defined facets, terminations, reconstructions, and chemical-potential conditions.
questions.prerequisites: Use a converged bulk reference and declare slab orientation, termination, area and multiplicity, thickness, vacuum, relaxation policy, and stoichiometric or chemical-potential convention.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This combines attributed published data with a synthetic bulk-drift diagnostic; it is not an end-to-end surface calculation.

questions.validation_requirement: Test slab thickness, vacuum, lateral sampling, bulk-reference drift, reconstruction, termination, relaxation depth, and asymmetric-slab treatment.
questions.claim_limitation: One slab energy does not establish equilibrium morphology, environmental stability, kinetics, or the experimentally realized termination.
questions.common_human_route: Build and visually inspect termination-aware slabs with a GUI or library, converge slab and bulk references comparably, then compare surface-energy ledgers.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect orientation, termination, stoichiometry, thickness, vacuum, dipoles, relaxation, reconstruction, energy convergence, and assumed surface equivalence.

questions.question: What is the work function of this surface?
questions.required_observable: A side-specific field-free vacuum potential plateau minus a compatible Fermi level from the same qualified slab calculation.
questions.prerequisites: Use a qualified slab, adequate vacuum, a controlled electrostatic profile, a declared dipole treatment, and clear identification of the surface side.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This uses a synthetic planar-potential fixture; it is not evidence for a real surface work function.

questions.validation_requirement: Check plateau flatness, vacuum and slab-thickness sensitivity, k-point sampling, Fermi-level identity, dipole correction, and inequivalent surface sides.
questions.claim_limitation: Work function is not surface energy and does not identify the stable facet, interface band alignment, or an experimental contact potential without the corresponding model.
questions.common_human_route: Inspect slab and vacuum direction visually, calculate electrostatic potential, plot planar or macroscopic averages, and identify a stable vacuum plateau relative to the Fermi level.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect vacuum thickness, plateau flatness, dipole corrections, side dependence, potential alignment, Fermi-level definition, and numerical sensitivity.

questions.question: How favorable is adsorption, and which site is preferred?
questions.required_observable: Comparable adsorption energies or free energies across declared sites, coverages, periodic cells, molecular references, and surface states.
questions.prerequisites: Prepare a qualified clean slab, adsorbate reference, enumerated starting sites, a coverage and cell convention, and compatible relaxed endpoint calculations.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This uses attributed and synthetic bookkeeping material; it is not an executed adsorption project.

questions.validation_requirement: Check site and state identity after relaxation, coverage, cell size, slab convergence, reference states, numerical convergence, and thermal or electrochemical corrections when claiming a free energy.
questions.claim_limitation: Negative adsorption energy does not establish catalytic activity, reaction rate, selectivity, poisoning resistance, or experimental adsorption conditions.
questions.common_human_route: Use a viewer or builder for several adsorption geometries, calculate slab, adsorbate, and combined systems comparably, then inspect structures and energy differences.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect sites, orientations, reconstruction, dissociation, image interactions, reference states, coverage, competing minima, forces, and comparability.

questions.question: Where did charge redistribute?
questions.required_observable: A difference density built from compatible component densities on the same cell, geometry, grid, and electronic convention, with an integral-closure check.
questions.prerequisites: Evaluate the combined and fragment densities with compatible geometry, cell, grid, basis or core treatment, occupations, and electron counts.

first_action.evidence_boundary: This uses invented compatible grids; it does not generate a real DFT density-difference chain.

questions.validation_requirement: Check grid and cell identity, electron-count convention, full-cell integral closure, interpolation control, and sensitivity to any charge-partition scheme.
questions.claim_limitation: Difference-density lobes do not define a unique transferred-electron count, bond order, oxidation state, or causal bonding mechanism. Partitioned charges remain method-dependent.
questions.common_human_route: Generate compatible combined and fragment densities, confirm identical cells and grids, construct the difference field, and inspect integrals plus isosurfaces or slices.
questions.what_to_inspect: Inspect grid and atom alignment, subtraction convention, charge closure, isovalue dependence, spatial localization, and model robustness.
